text:
maya: quick q — how do we want clients to observe a 'soft-expired' pin? do we return the pinned variant but flag it, or surface a different code path so clients can proactively refresh?
jun: imo we should avoid returning surprise models. flagging + header seems reasonable: keep serving but include `x-pin-state: soft-expired` so clients can decide.
liam: +1 for header, but watch for SDK behavior — we have clients that only swallow body and ignore headers.
sara: for Dedicated customers we promised no roll changes mid-commit, soft-expiry needs stricter semantics there. maybe a tenant override?
maya: good point. proposal: tenant-level policy that can opt-out of serving soft-expired variants; default behavior for hosted is header+serve.
liam: operationally, we need to ensure runtime fallback doesn't swap to a different variant silently. can we make the cache key include `pin_epoch` so serving infra can detect mismatches?
jun: adding `pin_epoch` to routing key is fine, but that makes caching less efficient for short-lived pins. tradeoff.
sara: Another angle — emit an audit event when a request hits a soft-expired pin, so console shows which clients are seeing degraded pins.
ava: from DevEx — exposing the header + an SDK helper that raises `PinSoftExpiredWarning` would nudge apps to refresh without breaking.
maya: +1 on SDK helper. also need clear docs: what 'soft' means (graceful evict window, no automatic rollback).
liam: what's the exact window? previously we discussed 5m eco grace then 24h tombstone. we should pick numbers and call them out in schema fields: `expiry_ts`, `soft_ttl_sec`, `hard_ttl_sec`.
jun: agree. schema proposal: `pin_meta: { pin_id, pinned_variant, expiry_ts, soft_ttl_sec, hard_ttl_sec, origin }` — but keep in mind agents.md earlier advice to avoid nested objects in transport; this is internal metadata though.
maya: for API surface let's flatten: `pin_id`, `pinned_variant`, `expiry_ts`, `soft_ttl`, `hard_ttl`, `origin`. keep units seconds.
sara: we also need clear compatibility contract for rollout metadata consumers. older clients should default to safe behavior (treat unknown `pin_state` as `soft-expired`?).
liam: safer to treat unknown or missing fields as `pinned` (no expiry) to preserve liveness. but that hides expiries from older clients — could be ok if we rely on telemetry to migrate.
jun: maybe version the rollout metadata: `rollout_meta_version: 2` and schema validators; older clients that don't understand v2 will get v1 and we can avoid surprises.
ava: ops concern — telemetry + billing spikes if clients start refreshing massively when they see `soft-expired`. recommend backoff guidance in SDK and console UX showing client counts.
maya: agreed. action items: 1) liam/infra: propose minimal routing key change and cache impact analysis (due EOD Wed) 2) jun/api: draft flattened schema with `rollout_meta_version` and header names (due Thu) 3) ava/devex: SDK helper + backoff guidance draft (Fri) 4) sara/product: tenant opt-out semantics doc for Dedicated (end of week)
sara: tagging ops: @deploy-bot can we add a telemetry flag for `soft_expiry_hit` so we can query by tenant?
deploy-bot: noted. I created ticket #INFR-1429 to emit `soft_expiry_hit` counter with tags: tenant_id, model, pin_id. ETA 2026-03-24.
maya: thanks. quick follow-up — how do we represent intentional pin deprecations vs accidental expiry? need an `intent` field?
jun: add `pin_reason` freeform string and `deprecation_flag: true|false`. defaults false.
liam: keep `pin_reason` short; don't rely on it for automation.
ava: I'll put a short example in SDK docs: header `x-pin-state: pinned|soft-expired|expired`, headers `x-pin-id`, `x-pin-epoch`, `x-rollout-meta-version`.
maya: perfect. last note: let's avoid new network roundtrips at request path. headers + telemetry + SDK helpers should be enough for 90% of cases. anyone object?
sara: no objections.
maya: thanks all — will capture notes and open the RFC follow-up PR with the flattened schema and example headers.
